newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ERG sees stronger H2 in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ERG sees stronger H2 in 1996/97.

text.p: ERG Ltd said it expects a stronger result in the second half of the year to June 30, 1997.
ERG earlier reported a 51.6 percent fall in net profit to A$6.47 million in the 1995/96 year.

"The directors remain confident that 1997 will see a strong rise in revenue and profitability, although both will be heavily weighted to the second half," ERG said in a statement accompanying its 1995/96 results.
ERG said the company's balance sheet remains strong with the debt to equity ratio at nine percent.
"The investment in new developments, new technology transfers and further upgrading of plant and equipment will all contribute to sharply higher revenue and profit in 1997," it said.
ERG sales rose 22.2 percent to A$159.19 million in 1995/96.
ERG said the drop in profitability was due to lower than forecast sales, and costs associated with phasing in new products, particularly in the telecommunications division.
In addition, total expenditure on research and development (R&D) increased to A$31.5 million or 19.8 percent of sales from A$22 million a year earlier, ERG said.
It said its telecommunications unit is currently finalising negotiations with ADC Telecommunications Inc of the United States for the start of production of ADC's products.
ERG is also to developing locally some mobile phone products of Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy.

"Due to the phased nature of these major technology transfers with both Nokia and ADC, the full benefit of the sales is not expected to start accruing to ERG until the second half of the 1997 financial year," ERG said.
At 2.05 p.m. (0405 GMT), ERG shares were one cent lower at A$1.41.
